media.title: Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929 — Jazz auf vier Flügeln review
media.description: Review titled ‘Jazz auf vier Flügeln — Zweites städtisches Sonderkonzert in Hamborn’ (signed Dr. Funk) in the Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929. It covers the First Piano Quartet (Erstes Klavier-Quartett) of four pianists — Bronisław Kaper, Leopold Mittmann, Alexander Zakin and Julian Pomeranc — performing on four grand pianos, including their own compositions. The programme ranged from Schubert, Verdi, Strauss, Kreisler and Rimsky-Korsakov to the ‘Blue Danube’ and modern dances; Kaper contributed a tango for four grand pianos (Vierflügeltango), and Mittmann a Jazz-Prélude and three ‘Jazz-Babies’.
media.altText: German newspaper review headed “Jazz auf vier Flügeln.”
media.rightsNote: The review was published in 1929 and is in the public domain in the United States. It is signed ‘Dr. Funk’; the author’s full identity and date of death have not been established, and copyright status outside the United States remains undetermined. The local copy is reduced to 768 × 800 px.

timelineEvents.title: ERKLA-Quartett concert review in Hamborn
timelineEvents.label: 10 Dec 1929 · ERKLA in Hamborn
timelineEvents.shortDescription: A Rhein- und Ruhrzeitung review documents Kaper’s appearance with the ERKLA four-piano ensemble in Hamborn, alongside Giuliano Pomeranz, then performing as Julian Pomeranc, Alexander Zakin, and Leopold Mittmann.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Dr. Funk’s review “Jazz auf vier Flügeln” in the Rhein- und Ruhrzeitung, evening edition, 10 December 1929, p. 2, documents an ERKLA concert in Hamborn. It names Kaper alongside Giuliano Pomeranz, then performing as Julian Pomeranc, Alexander Zakin, and Leopold Mittmann. Kaper joined the ensemble after Adam Gelbtrunk’s departure, at Leopold Mittmann’s urging; the announcements of the late 1920s otherwise list the quartet without him, so the association cannot be counted as a regular one. Dr. Funk credited him with a “Vierflügeltango” of sonorous linear writing and Mittmann with a “Jazz-Prélude” and three “Jazz-Babies”.

places.publicNote: Hamborn, in the Ruhr area, was the setting of the ERKLA concert reviewed in December 1929. The review named Kaper alongside Giuliano Pomeranz, then performing as Julian Pomeranc, Alexander Zakin and Leopold Mittmann.
